Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 6, 2021
Review Body:
I give this book five stars for its CONTENT but I felt it would be silly to take a whole star off just because of the publisher.

My only issues are small so I’ll just get them out of the way:
— Sentences are missing MANY commas, so I often have to reread to understand. But it’s worth it because this is the best psychology book I have EVER read, & I’ve only read a 100 pages!
— Softcover is super flimsy, pages are nearly as thin as bible paper. This makes it really hard to take notes in the book. I have my B.S in psych so I wanna use this as a reference when I make it to grad school. I wish it was closer to the size of a textbook.

ANYWAY!

I don’t even know where to start. I’ve read so many of the popular psychology/self-help books & still felt like something wasnt making sense about the trauma part. I have had a few traumatic experiences in childhood & I’m still figuring out how I feel about myself at 30yrs old.

If you think you have trauma, you probably do. It can be small. It does mot have to be a war zone or car accident to distort your thinking. Anyone who reads this book or considers it needs to understand this because you need to accept your trauma to let yourself move on. You deserve it!

This book is a cure for the curious. It’s the best manual for ANY person who seeks out therapy or wants to try to use self-educating. This book has everything you can think of related to trauma.

It will BLOW. YOUR. MIND. I consider myself fairly educated on the subject & I constantly find myself in awe of what the writer says.

This book is perfect for you or your family so they can help understand you & vice versa. I have been marking passages to show to my family. I don’t believe there is ANYONE who couldn’t benefit from this absolute masterpiece.

Go buy it. You will not regret it. I rarely buy physical copies of books but I HAD to have this one after reading it on my kindle. I am just in love with this book. I see myself buying another copy in the future just for notes.

P.S.- i wish Amazon would ban book reviews that give bad reviews based on how it arrived. Amazon will always help you out if you just go to the chat section!

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on November 18, 2018
Review Body:
I accidentally happened upon this book in search of a book I could both read on my kindle or listen to in my car. I had a lot of driving to do this month and I like the option of 'reading' when I can.
Its 5 star book high ranking book for a reason.
I had no idea what I was getting myself into when I began reading this. As an adult child of an alcoholic and one who likely suffers from complex PTSD, I was stunned to read the many decades of research that supports the authors main point. That the Body Keeps the Score of our trauma. While it was often difficult to read because of how much I related to the stories of so many traumatic lives being stuck in the deafening of the mind, I am glad I completed it and remain hopeful for my own recovery. I wish that more people would read it on the basis that we need to be more trauma aware of the lives that seem complicated around us and because it offers so much hope to those of us who suffer from a complex of trauma.
The first time I tried to kill myself, I was 3 years old. I jumped out of a moving vehicle because my dad was punching me while he was driving. I remember distinctly feeling worthless and wishing the cars tires would roll over me so that I could stop the pain. In becoming a mother, I fought many arguments with adults or other parents or the other parent of my children about my belief that all forms of corporal punishment weren't okay. I frustratingly put a spirited temper tantrum prone 2 year old in time-out time and time again to avoid the same hurt and pain I suffered as a child. I was hopeful that she might become better than me. That when her time to grow up came she wouldn't have a grey veil over her life that kept her from fulling living.
My spirited angry 2 year old with enough time and patience has become a 15 year old driven, attending a college prep high school, and showing great promise with a career in dance. She's level headed and kind. She works hard and doesn't need to be pushed.
I know it's hard to raise kids without feeling overwhelmed. I have felt overwhelmed a million times. I believe they can turn out okay with patience, love and time. The Body Keeps The Score, is proof of something I knew form my own abusive childhood memories. Love our kids. Don't hurt them.
I wish anyone who ever suffers from depression take the time to find the answers that I found here in this book. Thank you.

Review Body:
If you have had any trauma in your life I encourage you to read this. It is so well-written and engaging that I did not sleep all night after I started to read it. I stayed up listening to the audible version intermittently also reading the Kindle version and then I purchased a hard copy so I could share it with other others.

Despite my having learned previously that I have a very high ACE score, I did not really, fully understand the scope of the damage that was done to me, and how that is related to my many medical issues that have continued and even worsened over the decades.

Now I can see myself more clearly and this will help me to stop blaming myself for having to struggle so hard to feel normal. The author certainly understands me much better than I have ever understood myself. More importantly, there are the recommendations for recovery toward the end of the book. I would like him to write an entire book devoted to treatment programs and therapies.

Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 2, 2015
Review Body:
I bought this book to help me. The book is entirely and profoundly readable. Van der Kolk literally paints a visual picture to clue laypeople into just what the brain does, on trauma. I have found HUGE chunks of deeply meaningful information. I'm not done ... It becomes hard to digest because it hits intensely real feelings. If you, like me, *know* "talk therapy" isn't enough, and you want a sense of rational control over how to "deal with it"... This is your book.
1-Over and over, every critical point is clearly documented.
2- Straight truth about the +/-'s of medication.
3- History of how the world has/has not dealt with trauma - fascinating!
4- introduction to treatments that work.
5- How to find a therapist. BIG, because you want somebody EFFECTIVE.
6- With Kindle, you can literally Google a word from within the book and find awesome stuff!
